newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta shares end mixed on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta shares end mixed on short covering.

text.p: Share prices closed mixed at the Calcutta bourse on Wednesday as few select blue-chips steadied on short covering by local speculators, brokers said.

They said foreign institutional investors (FIIs) still remained out of the market and had placed no buy orders for large quantities. On the contrary they maintained selling pressure on some blue-chips.

But local speculators rushed to cover their short positions ahead of the end of the accounting period of the Calcutta bourse next Friday. With most large players like Indian mutual funds and foreign funds shying away from making fresh investments, volumes continued to look bad, dealers said.
"At the moment, the stock market looks very bad and prices are falling too fast," said Vinod Baid of broker Prudential Capital Markets Limited. "But in the long term a recovery is inevitable."

Brokers said that prices opened a shade higher and tended to move up amidst low volumes on short covering. But they did not stay long at higher levels in the absence of fresh investment buying from any quarter, brokers said.
